title: PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement central bid window opens (FERC ER26-3380)
source: NEWS: utilitydive.com/news/pjm-backstop-capacity-auction-ferc-data-centers/826792/ (published 2026-08-03, fetched direct 2026-09-08 HTTP 200) — PJM filed the Reliability Backstop Procurement at FERC on 2026-07-31 under docket ER26-3380-000, central bid window 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-21, results by 2026-12-02, against the 6,831 MW shortfall from the 2028/29 BRA. CORROBORATED ON THE FILING'S OWN PROCEDURAL POSTURE BY A FEDERAL PRIMARY: govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-06/html/2026-15979.htm (Combined Notice of Filings #1, fetched direct 2026-09-08 HTTP 200) lists 'PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.', '205(d) Rate Filing: Reliability Backstop Procurement to Address...', filed 7/31/26, accession 20260731-5214, EFFECTIVE DATE 9/29/2026, comments due 5 p.m. ET 8/21/26. Window-open date and mechanics corroborated by sysotechnologies.com/2026/08/21/pjm-reliability-backstop-procurement-rbp/ ('Sept. 30 - Oct. 21, 2026'; results 'December 2, 2026') and publicpower.org (APPA, 2026-07-31, 'commencing a Reliability Backstop Procurement (RBP) on Sept. 30, 2026'). Filed estimate on four counts: no FERC order, deficiency letter or suspension in ER26-3380 was found on any search run 2026-09-08 (recorded as an ABSENCE — elibrary.ferc.gov serves no document list to a plain fetcher and is in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked); PJM's own posted RPM page (pjm.com/markets-and-operations/rpm, fetched 2026-09-08 HTTP 200 by the proposing lane) carries no RBP schedule, so the confirmed `PJM:` prefix does not apply; the window opening is EXPRESSLY CONDITIONAL — PJM intends to open on 2026-09-30 only if the framework is accepted by 2026-09-29; and this calendar's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a Federal Register notice of a pending 205(d) filing
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-08 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, from proposals/pjm-reliability-backstop-procurement-2026-09-30.from-pjm-capacity-auction-2026-12.json (which it now shadows). TWO AMENDMENTS TO THE PROPOSAL, both sourced in docs/research/events/pjm-reliability-backstop-procurement-2026-09-30.md. (1) The proposal called $555/MW-day 'a price cap'. It is not a per-resource ceiling: it is a MW-WEIGHTED AVERAGE maximum willingness to pay across all selected offers (publicpower.org 2026-07-31, 'a MW-weighted average of $555/MW-day'; sysotechnologies 2026-08-21, 'a MW-weighted average cap of $555/MW-day across all selected offers'; kilowattlogic, 'volume-weighted maximum willingness to pay'), so an individual commitment may exceed $555 provided the selected portfolio averages at or under it. (2) The central procurement is PAY-AS-BID, not pay-as-clear ('Unlike the pay as clear structure of the RPM... the RBP will be structured as a pay as bid procurement' — sysotechnologies 2026-08-21; corroborated by renewableenergyworld's April design write-up, 'resources will get paid based on their offers/bids'), so this procurement cannot produce a uniform clearing price comparable to an RPM print. WHY 09-30 EARNS ITS ROW ANYWAY: it is the gate on the whole December sequence this calendar already tracks. Nothing is published that day — bids are confidential and the procurement target keeps moving (the bilateral target-adjustment window runs ~2026-09-10 to ~2026-10-09, overlapping the bid window) — so the only observable is binary: did PJM open at all. Impact medium and symbols empty on the proposing ledger's grounds: none of the nine tracked names is an IPP, the exposed names (VST/CEG/TLN/NRG) live in docs/research/ai-energy-constraint.md rather than on the tracked roster, and no house playbook is keyed to a capacity auction. Estimate — nothing here licenses a date-keyed entry.
